svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: A living register of every deliberate deviation from S88 / S95 / PackML — and why
broader than an industrial plant; enables the addressable path in Sub-model 11
“Zone” already means something specific in IEC 62443 (Sub-model 7)
S88 and S95 already use “segment” differently from each other
“Distributed” already means a DCS (multiple controllers) in OT usage
precise, standard network-topology term — needs no explanation
“Hybrid” already means continuous+batch manufacturing in S88
reuses existing Sub-model 4 state names instead of new, severity-implying labels
“Container” already means a Docker/Kubernetes deployment unit
plainer, more approachable — avoids a stuffy academic connotation
operator-response states are not object-behavior states — different question, different values
Alarm.source already means “which Device” (DeviceRef) — origin avoids a same-class field collision
manual override is universal, not exclusive to one mode (manualOverrideAvailable)
multi-CPU racks need Component granularity — Components already have id (Sub-model 1)
“site” is the Site level (Sub-model 2), “control” is ControlUnit — values name what the recipe is tied to
step names replaced by the Sub-model 2 level that runs them (area / cell / system / assembly)
“batch” only fits batch production — continuous, campaign and discrete runs need a neutral term
separate General / Site / Master / Control recipe types
one Recipe class; each recipe refines the one it was derived from, and recipeLevel says which level it is
“batch size” presumes discrete batches — a quantity or null also fits continuous and open-ended production
“role” means an RBAC Role in IAM (Sub-model 8) — a job title is not a permission set
“status” already means Rollup collective status (Sub-model 14) — own value space, like Alarm.state
bare “category” is ambiguous — this is the ISO 13849-1 designated architecture (B, 1–4)
“Policy” is already Simulation-, Retention- and security-policy elsewhere — this one governs change approval
“capability” already names the Topology flags and Operator capability (band 14–18)
bare “Security” collides with the whole Safety & Security band — the title now says what it models
renaming is not the default — these already fit LUNEX exactly as written in the source standard
not renamed from anything — these concepts simply don't exist in PackML or S88

a forward-looking claim, raised into the Alarm

STO / SS1 / SLS etc. per IEC 61800-5-2,

what was applied to which Device — gated

Rename a term only when it already carries a conflicting meaning elsewhere in the model, or in
an adjacent standard LUNEX must interoperate with. Otherwise, reuse established vocabulary —
inventing a new word is not innovation if the old one wasn't actually broken.
A term with a schema in Appendix A (a class or record) is written in CamelCase, in prose too: ControlUnit, SignalConverter, AlarmResponseProcedure.
Concepts and layers without a schema keep spaces: Digital Twin, Telemetry Envelope, Context Layer. Plural: “ControlUnit objects”, never “ControlUnits”.
